Alex — thanks for sending the forecast. We looked it over and have three pragmatic packaging options that typically fit this pattern. High level: all options can be co-termed to Jan 1 with pro-rated credits for the initial partial period.

Option 1 — Multi-year upfront (best unit economics):
- 3yr commitment, 15% list discount with full upfront prepay.
- Annual true-up (we reconcile actual tokens/embeddings at each anniversary).
- Pros: lowest unit cost, simpler billing. Cons: cash outlay upfront.

Option 2 — Phased annualization (recommended given your ramp):
- 3yr legal term, annualized commit percentages: Y1 40% of nominated peak, Y2 70%, Y3 100%.
- 20% upfront prepay on execution to reserve burst capacity in Year 1.
- Yearly true-ups with ability to accelerate ramp if usage exceeds thresholds (we apply credits to future invoices).
- Pros: aligns spend to product ramp, lowers Year 1 cash burden vs full prepay.

Option 3 — Hybrid reserve + burst buffer (ops-focused):
- 2yr term with option to add a dedicated burst pool for 6 months during launches.
- Moderate discount (8%), monthly billing for incremental burst usage.
- Pros: operational flexibility; Cons: higher unit price.

A few clarifying Qs to size the SOW and finalize pricing:
1) Can you confirm whether the attached forecast is conservative or optimistic vs expected traffic?
2) Do you need a hard SLA for dedicated capacity during ramp periods? If so, we can outline a capacity guarantee with a small premium.
3) Is co-terming to 2028-01-01 acceptable (that will be the default start for the aligned anniversaries)?

If you like Option 2, I can draft a short one-page summary showing invoice cadence, true-up examples, and the proposed prepay amount. From there we can route to procurement for PO / redlines.

Cheers,

Looping in ops notes from our side.

Mina — I agree Option 2 is the best fit. A couple of operational items to propose in writing so CloudScale knows what they'll get during Year 1 spike:
- Capacity buffer: include a 25% burst buffer on top of the Y1 committed baseline for 90 days post-launch; excess beyond that billed at a discounted burst rate.
- Ramp notification windows: CloudScale to notify 30 days before expected major traffic increases to let us schedule additional nodes.
- Fallback model: if dedicated capacity is constrained we will route to a compatible quantized variant (slightly slower) with guaranteed latency tiers — documented in the SOW.

Also, on discounts — we can ladder an additional 2% discount if the customer opts into a 12-month auto-renew at the end of Year 1 (effectively locking the price). That may be attractive if finance wants predictability.

Alex / Patricia — apologies for the slight delay; we've pulled together the one-pager and SOW. Summary of agreed commercial terms below (we will reflect these in the SOW / order form):

Agreed summary (commercial):
- Legal term: 3 years; Co-term effective date: 2028-01-01.
- Structure: Phased annualization (Y1 40% baseline, Y2 70%, Y3 100%).
- Prepay: 20% of Year 1 baseline due on signature; applied as credit across the first 12 months.
- Burst buffer: 25% capacity buffer for 90 days post major launch, billed at discounted burst rate if exceeded.
- Auto-renew: Renewal will auto-renew for 12 months unless customer provides written opt-out at least 60 days prior to the renewal anniversary. Opt-out preserves the right to re-negotiate terms but does not affect accrued credits.
- True-up: Annual true-up at each anniversary (prorated for co-term if applicable).
- SLA/Operations: Capacity ladder and fallback model included in SOW; Marcus will own any operational runbooks.

Next steps:
1) We've attached PHASED_ANNUALIZATION_SOW_v2.pdf with examples of invoice proration and a sample invoice showing Jan 1 co-term.
2) Patricia — please confirm procurement timing and any preferred PO templates. If acceptable, sign the order form and we will issue an invoice for the 20% prepay.
3) We'll add a HubSpot note (link below) with final terms and push for a May 5 kickoff for onboarding.
